personas.name: Doreen Achterberg
personas.background: Lives with her husband and a lodger who is a nursing student. Shops weekly at the same supermarket and keeps a paper list on the fridge.
personas.history: Was signed up to a magazine subscription she could not cancel online and had to phone three times. Now distrusts anything that asks for a card 'for free'.
personas.lens: Can someone with poor eyesight and no patience for apps get through the first screen at all?

personas.name: Kwame Asante
personas.background: Shares a five-person student flat where milk theft is a running feud. Pays for everything with a debit card that often sits near zero.
personas.history: Has installed and abandoned three flat-chore apps; the flat now uses a group chat with pinned messages.
personas.lens: Would a broke student flat actually adopt this instead of the group chat?

personas.name: Marisol Quintero
personas.device: older iPhone, cracked screen, patchy mobile data
personas.background: Feeds a household of five on a tight budget, shops at two stores to chase deals, and reads English slowly when tired.
personas.history: Lost money to a 'free trial' that renewed annually without warning. Checks every price twice.
personas.lens: Is the real price clear in plain English to someone reading it as a second language on a small screen?

personas.name: Harald Nygaard
personas.background: Arrived on the site by mistake from a search for a pantry shelving unit. Lives alone, cooks properly, wastes little.
personas.history: Has no problem with technology but dislikes being sold subscriptions for things a notebook does.
personas.lens: The wildcard: someone outside the target market who arrived by accident.

personas.name: Priya Raman
personas.role: operations lead at a small meal-prep company
personas.device: MacBook, then iPhone in the kitchen
personas.background: Runs stock for a 12-person kitchen that delivers 600 meals a week. Looking for anything that cuts waste without a big system.
personas.history: Currently runs inventory on a shared Google Sheet with conditional formatting for expiry. Her director signs off any spend over a few hundred pounds a year.
personas.current_tool: Google Sheets with expiry colour rules
personas.lens: Can a household app stretch to a tiny commercial kitchen, and can she justify it to her director?

personas.name: Tom Okafor
personas.role: property manager for shared student housing
personas.background: Manages 40 shared houses. Kitchen disputes and food left to rot are a top cause of complaints and deposit deductions.
personas.history: Pays for a facilities ticketing tool he dislikes. Would only consider something he can roll out per house and bill to the landlord.
personas.current_tool: nothing for kitchens; a ticketing system for repairs
personas.lens: Could this be bought per house by a landlord or letting agent, and who owns the data then?

personas.name: Hannah Brooks
personas.background: Plans meals on Sunday, already pays for a recipe app and a grocery delivery membership. Buys for a family of four.
personas.history: Happy user of a competing list app that her husband also uses; switching would mean convincing him.
personas.lens: Comparison shopper who already owns a competing product and is happy with it.

personas.name: Jordan Ellis
access_needs: ADHD, loses focus on long forms
personas.background: Lives with a partner; both forget what is in the fridge and throw food out weekly. Impulse buyer of apps that promise to fix habits.
personas.history: Has a graveyard of habit-app subscriptions and now cancels anything that bills annually.
personas.lens: Impulse buyer with ADHD: does the flow keep their attention long enough to buy?

personas.name: Linh Tran
personas.role: accountant, buying for her elderly parents
personas.background: Shops for her parents, who live 20 minutes away, and worries about them eating expired food. Deal hunter who reads every footnote.
personas.history: Uses loyalty apps for discounts but has opted out of every data-sharing option she has ever been offered.
personas.lens: Buying for someone else, privacy-conscious deal hunter.

personas.name: Ines Corvalan
personas.background: Advises consumer apps on GDPR. Reads privacy pages for a living and knows the gap between 'anonymised' and 'aggregated'.
personas.history: Has handled two regulator complaints about retail data sharing dressed up as 'offers'.
personas.lens: Lawful basis and data flows for receipt data and partner sharing.

personas.name: Gareth Pryce
personas.background: Works on subscription traps and drip pricing. Tracks how trials convert and how prices are displayed.
personas.history: Spent a decade at a consumer advice body before private practice; still thinks like a complaints handler.
personas.lens: Price display, card-required trials and auto-renewal to an annual plan.

personas.name: Sana Mirza
personas.role: consumer technology reporter at an independent tech newsletter
personas.background: Covers subscription apps and the ad-tech behind them. Writes a monthly column on dark patterns.
personas.history: Her most-read piece was about a budgeting app that sold transaction data; she now reads every privacy page before every launch story.
personas.seat: technology journalist who covers this category
personas.lens: Is there a story here, and is the story the data, not the pantry?

personas.name: Rebecca Lund
personas.background: Backs consumer subscription apps at pre-seed. Former growth lead at a meal-kit company.
personas.history: Saw meal-kit retention collapse after promotions ended; obsessive about cohort retention and household-level virality.
personas.seat: seed or pre-seed VC from the product's home region
personas.lens: Does the household invite loop create retention that a single-user app cannot?

personas.name: Daniel Hoffmann
personas.role: angel investor, former grocery retail executive
personas.background: Spent 20 years in grocery retail, last as head of loyalty at a large chain. Invests 25-50k EUR per deal.
personas.history: Built a loyalty data business and knows exactly what retailers pay for basket data and what they refuse to pay for.
personas.seat: angel with an operating background in exactly this domain
personas.lens: Is the partner-offers revenue real, and would retailers buy this data?

personas.name: Aiko Matsuda
personas.background: Series A investor in consumer and fintech. Publicly skeptical of 'save money' consumer apps whose savings are never measured.
personas.history: Passed on a dozen food-waste startups; the two she watched fail died on retention after month three.
personas.seat: hostile specialist, on record as a skeptic of this category
personas.lens: Food-waste apps churn: what is different here, measured?
